key_insight: RoboTTT shows that robot policies can use extremely long visuomotor context—up to 8K timesteps—without increasing inference latency. This unlocks new capabilities like one-shot imitation from human videos and online policy improvement.
problem_solved: Most robot foundation models only use single-step or short-history context, which limits how much past experience they can use to understand demonstrations, adapt on the fly, and stay robust under changing conditions.
method: Introduces Test-Time-Training Robot Policies (RoboTTT), a model and training recipe designed for very long visuomotor context.
Scales policy context length to 8K timesteps, roughly three orders of magnitude beyond prior state-of-the-art.
Uses test-time training so the model can adapt from context without increasing inference latency.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a practical path to more capable and adaptable robot policies without paying a runtime cost. It could make imitation learning, recovery from errors, and deployment in dynamic environments much more effective.
visual_elements: A timeline or context-length bar showing 8K timesteps vs. short-history baselines.

paper_title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
paper_authors: Yunfan Jiang, Yevgen Chebotar, Ruijie Zheng, Fengyuan Hu, Yunhao Ge
